title: Fourier component as a coefficient sum
statement: Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, and let $(\psi_a)_{a\in\iota}$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product. For $n\in\mathbb N$, a function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and a coordinate set $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, its Fourier component supported on $S$ equals the sum, over all multi-indices $a\in\iota^n$ whose nonconstant coordinates are exactly $S$, of its Fourier coefficient at $a$ times the product basis function $x\mapsto\prod_{i=1}^n\psi_{a_i}(x_i)$.
hypotheses_covered: Basis is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product
